title: Lantern and Harbor
premise: In the port city of Vessany, on the eve of a revolution that will redraw the coastline and its loyalties, Lior Ishikawa works in her father's print shop, setting type for a regime she quietly despises. When an infant is abandoned at their door with a note reading 'forget the face,' the family's careful invisibility shatters: the child belongs to a hunted dissident printer whose plates Lior's father once engraved. As the revolution burns toward armistice, Lior discovers the last evacuation berth out of the harbor can hold only one of them — and the choice between her father, the child, and the man she has come to love forces her to decide whether survival means forgetting faces or finally being seen. In the end, Lior gives up her own berth, stays behind to print the truth as the armistice is signed, and rebuilds the shop into a harbor of memory rather than escape.
about_author: Rafael Whitlock is the pen name of a former typesetter who spent a decade restoring letterpress equipment in coastal archives before turning to fiction. Their novels examine how ordinary trades become extraordinary witnesses to history.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. We meet the Ishikawa print shop: father Elias cutting typefaces, mother dead three winters, Lior setting government proclamations by lamplight. She believes revolutions happen in capitals, not harbors. Emotional beat: the comfort of routine, shadowed by a censor's new inspection notice nailed to the door.

chapters.title: A Knock Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. An infant is left at the door in a fish crate, wrapped in a page printed from a forbidden plate — one Elias recognizes as his own early engraving. The note says only 'forget the face.' Emotional beat: fear cracking open curiosity; the first lie Lior tells an official.

chapters.title: What the Censor Reads
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Flashback woven through present: twenty years ago Elias engraved plates for dissident printer Tomas Verel, then bought silence by testifying he never knew him. Now the child may be Tomas's granddaughter. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing like ink stains that never wash out.

chapters.title: Milk and Gunpowder
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The household adapts to the baby, named Nell by Lior against all advice to remain unattached. Neighbor smuggler Dario Ferro supplies milk and warnings: the harbor closes in six weeks when the armistice talks conclude. Emotional beat: tenderness becoming dangerous.

chapters.title: The Inspector's Eye
chapters.summary: Inspector Corvane's POV. A regime man who genuinely loves typography, Corvane inspects the shop and lingers over a typeface he swears he's seen before. He leaves unconvinced but charmed by Lior. Emotional beat: menace wearing a courteous mask.

chapters.title: Letters to No One
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior secretly prints leaflets at night using Tomas's recovered plate, testing whether she is her father's daughter or something braver. Dario helps distribute them; attraction sparks between practical jokes about kerning. Emotional beat: exhilaration of first transgression.

chapters.title: The Harbor List
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Evacuation berths are allocated by trade and loyalty; Elias's engraver status earns exactly one seat on the final ship before the armistice seals the port. He hides the letter from Lior. Emotional beat: a father's love curdling into secrecy.

chapters.title: Faces in the Crowd
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. At a market protest Lior sees a woman who looks startlingly like Nell might at thirty — Tomas's daughter Mara, alive and searching. Lior says nothing, terrified of losing the child. Emotional beat: the first taste of moral compromise she chose herself.

chapters.title: Corvane Returns
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. A leaflet reaches the ministry; Corvane recognizes the plate work instantly. He returns to the shop under pretense of ordering wedding invitations, watching Lior's hands. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse where both parties suspect the other knows.

chapters.title: The Room Above the Shop
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior and Dario's romance deepens in stolen hours; he reveals he's ferrying fugitives and could take Nell out early — but only the baby, alone. Lior refuses. Emotional beat: love asking for a price she isn't ready to pay.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias confesses everything to Lior: his testimony against Tomas, the berth, his plan to take it himself and send money back. Lior's fury opens old wounds about her mother's death during the last purge. Emotional beat: family fracture along the fault line of survival.

chapters.title: Mara at the Door
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Mara finds the shop, half-dead, and confirms Nell is her daughter, left behind so she could lead rebels through the marshes. She asks for the child back — or for Lior to keep her safe forever, whichever the night allows. Emotional beat: two mothers' claims colliding without malice.

chapters.title: Three Names on One Berth
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The arithmetic becomes brutal: one berth, four candidates — Elias, Nell, Mara (now hunted), and Lior herself if she abandons the press. Each argues for another. Emotional beat: love measured in logistics, unbearable and precise.

chapters.title: The Plate in the Wall
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Soldiers raid neighboring shops; Elias hides Tomas's original plates inside the typecase wall, knowing discovery means execution. Corvane arrives early, alone, and — seeing the hidden seam — says nothing, leaving a single word chalked on the door: 'Soon.' Emotional beat: dread suspended by an enemy's unreadable mercy.

chapters.title: What Forgetting Costs
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior attempts the note's instruction — burning the evidence, preparing to forget — and cannot. She prints five hundred copies of the armistice's secret terms, which prove the regime plans to renege on amnesty. Emotional beat: identity chosen over safety, irrevocably.

chapters.title: Betrayal, Small and Human
chapters.summary: Dario's POV. Under torture-threat after a crewmate breaks, Dario's route is exposed. He must choose between warning the Ishikawas and moving his remaining passengers. He rows through gunfire to do both and takes a bullet in the shoulder. Emotional beat: loyalty proven in blood, imperfectly.

chapters.title: The Last Night of the Harbor
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Armistice signing at dawn; the final ship loads at midnight. Corvane comes not to arrest but to offer Lior the berth he was allotted, calling it 'a collector's respect for fine work.' She realizes even censors are people choosing sides. Emotional beat: the climax's terrible generosity.

chapters.title: One Berth
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging at the dock. Lior puts Mara and Nell aboard together, sends Elias to steer the press underground inland with Dario, and steps back onto the pier as the gangplank rises. Emotional beat: the choice made — she keeps no one's place but her own among the forgotten.

chapters.title: Printing the Dawn
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Alone with the presses as the armistice is signed, Lior prints ten thousand copies of the true terms and scatters them from the harbor steps while soldiers hesitate to fire on a girl holding paper, not weapons. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Wet Ink
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Ordered to execute the printer, Corvane instead reports the shop destroyed, falsifying his own record for the first time. He walks past Lior in the crowd and does not see her — or chooses not to. Emotional beat: an enemy's quiet defection.

chapters.title: The Face Remembered
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, one year later. The war's aftermath brings refugees, and among them letters from Mara: Nell's first words include 'press.' Lior reopens the shop openly, hanging the forbidden plate above the door. Emotional beat: grief settling into legacy.

chapters.title: Lantern and Harbor
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, years later. Elias returns gray-haired; Dario stays for good; a grown Nell sets her first crooked line of type. Lior lights the shop lantern each night facing the sea — a signal to every face the world asked her to forget. Emotional beat: home as an act of remembrance, complete.
